short: An Athenian historian and general whose work is a foundational text of political science.
full:
Thucydides was an Athenian historian and general whose History of the Peloponnesian War recounts the fifth-century BC war between Sparta and Athens. He has been dubbed the father of "scientific history" by those who accept his claims to have applied strict standards of impartiality and evidence-gathering, and of analysing cause and effect without reference to intervention by the deities. His work remains a core text for the study of international relations.

Having served as a general, Thucydides was exiled from Athens after failing to prevent the Spartan capture of Amphipolis in 424 BCE. This exile allowed him to travel freely and associate with Peloponnesians, giving him a broader perspective on the conflict. His narrative focuses intensely on the mechanics of power, human nature, and political realism, using reconstructed speeches to illuminate the motives of the actors. His analytical rigour set a new standard for historical writing that contrasted sharply with the more expansive style of Herodotus.
